title: Greatest Common Divisor
description: Read two non-negative integers and print their greatest common divisor (GCD). Implement the Euclidean algorithm in a function.
input_format: Two non-negative integers separated by whitespace; they are not both zero.

learning_content.title: Functions and reusable logic
learning_content.intro: A function groups a task into a named block that can receive parameters and return a result. The Euclidean algorithm repeatedly replaces (a, b) with (b, a mod b).
points: Define a function that accepts two integers.
While the second value is not zero, calculate the remainder.
Move the second value into the first position.
Move the remainder into the second position.
Return the first value when the loop ends.
learning_content.complexity: O(log(min(a, b))) time · O(1) extra space
learning_content.note: The Euclidean algorithm reduces the problem size quickly.

quiz.question: In the Euclidean algorithm, what pair replaces (a, b) during each iteration?

options.label: (a + b, a)
options.feedback: Adding the values is not the Euclidean remainder step.

options.label: (b, a mod b)
options.feedback: The old second value becomes the first, and the remainder becomes the second.

options.label: (a - b, b)
options.feedback: Subtraction is not the update used in this modulo-based version.

options.label: (a / b, b)
options.feedback: Integer division does not preserve the Euclidean algorithm invariant.

quiz.explanation: The update is (a, b) ← (b, a mod b).
